text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said Monday it will grant to Watson Pharmaceuticals Inc for about $190 million plus royalties an exclusive license to its Dilacor XR drug, used to treat hypertension and angina.
The company said the licensing period is four and a half years.
The deal includes a prepayment for the option to purchase the rights at the conclusion of the licensing period.
The agreement excludes certain non-U.S. markets in which Rhone-Poulenc currently markets Dilacor XR.
During the licensing period, Watson will pay an annual licensing fee and a royalty on sales.
Dilacor XR has been available for the treatment of hypertension since June 1992, and was approved for the treatment of chronic stable angina in March 1995 in the U.S.
